title: Navigating Tricks
intro: Getting the playhead and the view where you want them, instantly, is the difference between working and fiddling.

tips.d: Hold ⌃⌥ and drag a box around any part of the arrangement to zoom straight to it. Hold ⌃⌥ and click empty space to zoom back out.

src.label: Apple — Zoom windows in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Know what the number keys actually do
tips.d: The number keys recall screensets, not markers — Apple's guide says you recall a screenset by pressing any numeric key except 0, so 1–9 switch window layouts. If you want marker jumps on a key, open Key Commands (⌥K) and search “Go to Marker Number” — there are 20 of them, numbered by the order the markers appear in the project.

tips.d: If your Mac has a trackpad that supports gestures, you can scroll and zoom the Tracks area with gestures instead of reaching for the scrollbars. On a Mac with a Touch Bar, swipe left or right on the Touch Bar to scroll through the visible area of the project.

src.label: Apple — Scroll and zoom in the Tracks area in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use the Cycle area as a bookmark
tips.d: Select the region or passage you are working on and press U (Set Rounded Locators by Regions/Events and Enable Cycle). Logic sets the left and right locators around the selection, rounded, and turns Cycle on, so the cycle area marks your work area. Use ⌘U instead if you want the locators set by the selection without rounding.

tips.t: Toggle Catch to stop the screen running away
tips.d: With Catch on, the visible section of a window follows the playhead during playback. For detailed editing, click the Catch button in the Tracks area (or editor) menu bar to turn it off, and the view holds still. If it keeps switching back on, check Logic Pro > Settings > General > Catch: “Catch when starting playback” and “Catch when moving playhead” re-enable it.
